title: Number the lines of a text

blocks.text:
Java 11's `String.lines()` returns a `Stream<String>` of lines, splitting on `
`, `
` **and** ``, which `split("
")` does not. The page's edge cases: `lines()` on an empty string has **no** lines, and a trailing line terminator does **not** add an empty last line. `String.repeat(n)` builds padding without a loop (`"x".repeat(0)` is `""`).

Write `Listing.number(String text)`. It returns each line of `text` as `"<n>: <line>"`, numbering from 1. Blank lines in the middle are kept and numbered. When there are ten or more lines, **right-align** the numbers: pad each number on the left with spaces to the width of the largest one.

cases.says: Each line comes back as "<n>: <line>", counting from 1, blank inner lines included.
\n, \r\n and a lone \r all end a line, and none of them is left in the text.
A final line terminator ends the last line without adding an empty one, but an empty line before it is kept.
The empty text has no lines at all.
With ten or more lines (or a hundred or more), the shorter numbers are padded with spaces on the left to the widest number.

concepts: lines() gives no lines for an empty string and no trailing empty line after a final terminator.
